sections.HERBS AND ACTIONS:
Pharmaceutical Latin
Pin Yin
Dosage
Actions
Rx. Angelicae Sinensis
Dang Gui
3-15g
Tonifies, invigorates
and harmonizes the Blood, disperses Cold, stops pain due to
Blood Stasis and regulates
the menses.
With Bai Shao, regulates and harmonizes Qi and Blood and treats Blood Deficiency
Heat.
With Gan Cao, moderates spasms and relieves abdominal
pain.
With Xiang Fu, tonifies Blood and moves Qi, for
premenstrual symptoms, menstrual pain and irregular menstruation.
With Chuan Xiong, harmonizes, nourishes and invigorates
the Blood and disperses Blood Stasis.
With Dang Gui, for Blood Deficiency causing menstrual
problems including dysmenorrhea, scanty menses, and amenorrhea.
With Sheng Di Huang and Bai Shao, for headache
due to Blood Deficiency.
Rx. Rehmanniae
Sheng Di Huang
5-30g
Clears Heat, cools the Blood, nourishes Yin and generates
fluids.
With E Jiao, for coughing, hematemesis, epistaxis,
and uterine hemorrhage due to Heat from Deficiency.
With Bai Shao, for Blood Deficiency Heat.
Rx. Paeoniae Alba
Bai Shao
5-30g
Nourishes the Blood, astringes Yin, softens
the Liver, relieves pain and r egulates
menstruation.
With Gan Cao, regulates the relationship between
the Liver and Spleen.
With Sheng Di Huang and E Jiao, for Internal
Stirring of Liver Wind, as in the aftermath of a febrile disease.
With Dang Gui, nourishes Yin and
Blood.
Rz. Chuanxiong
Chuan Xiong
3-10g
Invigorates the Blood, promotes
the movement of Qi and a lleviates
pain.
With Xiang Fu, for Qi Stagnation combined
with Blood Stasis.
Rz. Anemarrhenae
Zhi Mu
6-12g
Clears Heat, drains Fire , nourishes Yin ,
moistens Dryness and clears
Deficiency Fire.
Rz. Coptidis
Huang Lian
1.5-10g
Clears Heat, drains Dampness and
stops bleeding.
With Zhi Mu, for Blazing Stomach Fire with intense
hunger, dry stools, dry, yellow tongue coat and a slippery rapid pulse.
With E Jiao and Bai Shao, for insomnia and irritability
due to overwhelming Heart Fire and Yin and Blood Deficiency.
Polygonati
Huang Jing
6-30g
Tonifies Spleen Qi, nurtures
Stomach Yin , tonifies the Kidneys and
strengthens Jing.
With Dang Gui, for Kidney Jing and
Blood Deficiency.
Cx. Phellodendri
Huang Bai
3-12g
Drains Damp-Heat especially from
the Lower Jiao and drains Deficiency
Heat.
With Zhi Mu, for
Yin Deficiency fever with steaming bones and night
sweats
and Lower Jiao Damp-Heat.
Colla Corii Asini
E Jiao
3-16g
Tonifies and nourishes the
Blood, stops
bleeding and nourishes
and moistens Yin.
With Bai Shao and Ai Ye, for
excessive menstrual bleeding.
With Huang Lian, for Heat toxin clumping in the Intestines,
injuring the Blood collaterals causing Blood and pus in the stools
especially during pregnancy or postpartum.
Hb. Artemisiae Argyi
Ai Ye
3-10g
Warms the channels, warms the womb,
s tops bleeding, calms the
fetus, disperses Cold and alleviates pain.
With E Jiao , for
heavy, painful periods due to Cold obstruction
and prolonged uterine bleeding and menorrhagia.
With Xiang Fu, for abdominal pain from Deficiency Cold
and Stagnant Qi.
With E Jiao, Dang Gui, Bai Shao, Sheng Di Huang, Gan Cao and Chuan
Xiong, for unstable pregnancy with vaginal bleeding due to
Deficiency Cold.
With Xiang Fu, Chuan Xiong, Dang Gui and Bai Shao, for
Deficiency Cold of the Lower Jiao with Cold and pain and
irregular menstruation with pain.
Rz. Cyperi
Xiang Fu
6-14g
Spreads and regulates Liver Qi, regulates
menstruation and a lleviates pain.
With Dang Gui and Chuan Xiong, for
irregular menstruation and dysmenorrhea due to Qi and
Blood Stasis.
Rx. Glycyrrhizae
Gan Cao
3-6g
Tonifies the Spleen and augments Qi and
moderates and harmonizes the harsh properties of other herbs.

sections.CONTRAINDICATIONS:
CONTRAINDICATIONS
Contraindicated for those with Excess above and deficiency below.
Contraindicated for those with Liver Fire.
Contraindicated for those with bleeding gums.
Use with caution for those with Liver Yang Rising.
Use with caution for those with hypertension.
Use with caution for those with hematemesis due to Yin Deficiency .
Use with caution for those with Yin and/or Blood Deficiency .
HERB/DRUG INTERACTIONS
Acute Pneumonitis maybe associated with interferon in combination with this formula.
Concurrent use of this formula and Interleukin 2 may have a synergistic anti-tumor effect against murine renal cell carcinoma.
Concurrent use of this formula and antiviral drugs such as zidovudine (AZT), lamivudine (3TC), or AZT plus 3TC may have a synergistic antiviral effect.
Concurrent use of this formula and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) may have a synergistic in treating of cancer.
This formula has a beneficial effect in preventing and/or treating damage induced by drugs such as halothane, danazol, D-galactosamine, and carbon tetrachloride.

sections.CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS:
Eruptions usually involve the flexor surfaces of the
wrists and forearms, and the lower legs around and above
the ankles.
Lesions manifest as intensely pruritic 2-10
mm flat-topped dull red shiny papules.
The surface of
the lesions exhibits a lacy white pattern of lines (Wickham’s
striae).
Lesions that persist, most frequently on the
shins, may develop into confluent hypertrophic
plaques that can resemble the lesions of lichen simplex
chronicus, with a coarse surface covered by scales.
Mucous
membranes are involved in 40-60% of lichen planus cases.
sections.NOTES: Decoct and administer one-half in the morning and one-half in the evening. Save the dregs, decoct again and use the fluid in a warm compress to be applied to the affected area for 10-15 minutes once daily. After two weeks, reduce both the Internal and External dosages to once every other day.

sections.HERBS AND ACTIONS:
Pharmaceutical Latin
Pin Yin
Dosage
Actions
Hb. Schizonepetae
Jing Jie
1-10g
Releases the exterior, expels Wind, vents rashes, and relieves itching.
With Niu Bang Zi and Chan Tui, for initial-stage measles and skin eruptions - brings rash to the surface and alleviates itching.
With Fang Feng, for pruritic itching, Exterior Excess and initial-stage boils.
With Fang Feng, Niu Bang Zi and Chan Tui , opens pores and disperses Wind.
With Dang Gui, for itching, and tremors of the hands and feet from Wind due to Blood Deficiency.
Rx. Saposhnikoviae
Fang Feng
2-10g
Releases the exterior, moves Qi , expels Wind-Cold-Dampness and a lleviates pain .
With Cang Zhu , for pain due to Wind-Dampness.
With Jing Jie and Chan Tui, for dermatological disorders with rash, irritability and itching.
Fr. Arctii
Niu Bang Zi
2-6g
Disperses Wind-Heat, benefits the throat, clears Internal Heat and vents rashes.
With Chan Tui, for weeping ulcers.
Periostracum Cicadae
Chan Tui
1-3g
Expels Wind, clears internal Heat and vents rashes.
With Jing Jie, Fang Feng and Ku Shen, for weepy red skin lesions in patients with pre-existing Damp-Heat.
Rz. Atractylodis
Cang Zhu
2-10g
Strongly dries Dampness and expels Wind-Dampness.
With Ku Shen and Mu Tong , for leakage of Fluids.
Rx. Sophorae Flavescentis
Ku Shen
1-6g
Clears Heat, dries Dampness, disperses Wind and stops itching.
With Chan Tui and Jing Jie , for generalized itching.
Caulis Akebiae
Mu Tong
1.5-6g
Drains Damp-Heat through the urine.
With Dang Gui, promotes circulation of Blood and stops pain.
Gypsum Fibrosum
Shi Gao
3-15g
Clears Heat, drains Fire and heals eczema, burns and ulcerated sores and wounds.
With Zhi Mu , clears Qi -level Heat and helps prevent the disorder from deepening.
With Sheng Di Huang, for excessive Fire with injured fluids.
With Sheng Di Huang and Zhi Mu, for Stomach Fire.
Rx. Anemarrhenae
Zhi Mu
1.5-6g
Clears Heat, drains Fire, nourishes Yin and moistens Dryness.
With Shi Gao , for epidemic diseases.
Rx. Rehmanniae
Sheng Di Huang
3-15g
Cools Blood and clears Heat.
Rx. Angelicae Sinensis
Dang Gui
3-10g
Nourishes and invigorates Blood, expels pus, reduces swelling and generates flesh.
Sm. Sesame
Hei Zhi Ma
1.5-15g
Nourishes Yin and Blood.
(Sm. Cannabis)
(Huo Ma Ren)
(1.5-15g)
(Substitutes for He Zhi Ma .)
Rx. Glycyrrhizae
Gan Cao
1-3g
Clears Heat, relieves toxicity and moderates and harmonizes the harsh properties of other herbs.
With Niu Bang Zi, strongly clears throat and Lungs to treat Wind-Heat attacks the Lungs or Fire toxin flaring upwards.

sections.CONTRAINDICATIONS:
CONTRAINDICATIONS
Avoid foods which are thought to stimulate Wind, such as alcohol, coffee, spicy foods, seafood, as well as smoking, while taking this formula.
Contraindicated for those with marked Qi or Blood Deficiency.
HERB/DRUG INTERACTIONS
sections.NOTES: This formula may be taken internally or applied topically.

CONTRAINDICATIONS
Do not use long term.
Contraindicated for those with Heat conditions.
Contraindicated for those with hemoptysis.
Contraindicated for those with coughing due to Yin Deficiency.
Contraindicated for those with dry mouth and throat with thick, yellow sputum.

Use with caution for those with hypertension.

The combination of inhaled fluticasone and this formula can be an important modality in the treatment of mild and severe asthma patients.

sections.HERBS AND ACTIONS:
Pharmaceutical Latin
Pin Yin
Dosage
Actions
Gypsum Fibrosum
Shi Gao
30g
Clears Heat in the Qi Stage, drains Fire, relieves irritability, quenches thirst, clears Excess Heat from the Lungs and clears Blazing Stomach Fire.
With Ren Shen, for excessive Heat with Qi Deficiency.
with Ren Shen and Mai Men Dong, for excessive Heat with Qi and Yin Deficiency.
Rz. Polygonati
Huang Jing
15g
Tonifies Spleen Qi, nurtures Stomach Yin, moistens Lung Yin , tonifies the Kidneys, strengthens Jing and relieves wasting and thirsting .
With Ren Shen, for weakness and debility, reduced appetite, fatigue and emaciation in the aftermath of a prolonged illness or as a result of a chronic wasting disease.
With Shi Gai, Tian Hua Fen, Shi Gao and Huang Lian, for wasting and thirsting disorder with relatively more Heat.
Rx. Paeoniae Alba
Bai Shao
15g
Nourishes the Blood, astringes Yin, adjusts the Ying and Wei, softens the Liver and relieves pain.
Rx. Dioscoreae
Shan Yao
15g
Tonifies the Spleen, nourishes Stomach, Lung and Kidney Yin. t onifies Lung Q i and astringes Jing.
With Shi Gao, Tian Hua Fen, Mai Men Dong and
Zhi Mu, for wasting and thirsting disorder ( Xiao Ke) with Internal Heat.
Rx. Polygoni Multiflori
He Shou Wu
15g
Tonifies the Liver and Kidneys, nourishes the Blood and nourishes Jing .
Rz. Anemarrhenae
Zhi Mu
9g
Clears Heat and drains Fire from the Lungs and Stomach Nourishes Yin and moistens Dryness G enerates Fluids, clears Deficiency Fire and quenches thirst.
With Huang Lian, for Blazing Stomach Fire with intense hunger, dry stools, dry, yellow tongue coat and a slippery rapid pulse.
With Tian Hua Fen and Mai Men Dong , for thirst and irritability due to Lung and Stomach Dryness.
With Shi Gao, cools Heat in the Yang Ming or Qi Level while protecting Stomach fluids to treat high fever, profuse sweating, insatiable thirst, a red face, aversion to Heat and a large, strong pulse.
Rz. Coptidis
Huang Lian
9g
Clears Heat, drains Dampness , drains Stomach Fire and resolves toxicity.
Colla Corii Asini
E Jiao
9g
Tonifies the Blood, nourishes and moistens Yin and moistens the Lungs and Large Intestine.
With Huang Lian, for Heat toxin clumping in the Intestines and injuring the Blood collaterals causing Blood and pus in the stools.
Rx. Trichosanthis
Tian Hua Fen
9g
Drains Heat, generates Fluids, clears and drains Lung Heat, transforms Phlegm and moistens Lung Dryness.
Rx. Ophiopogonis
Mai Men Dong
9g
Moistens the Lungs, nourishes Stomach Yin, moistens the Intestines and generates Fluids.
Cx. Lycii
Di Gu Pi
9g
Cools the Blood, drains Yin Deficiency Fire, drains Kidney Fire, eliminates lurking Heat and clears and drains Heat in the Lung.
Rx. Ginseng
Ren Shen
5g
Tonifies Yuan Qi , Spleen, Stomach and Lung Qi , generates Body Fluids and stops thirst .
With Shi Gao and Zhi Mu, for Heat injuring the Qi and Yin fluids with fever, irritability, intense thirst and profuse sweating.
with Mai Men Dong, Tian Hua Fen and Zhi Mu, for wasting and thirsting disorder with intense unquenchable thirst.

sections.NOTES:
Remove the shells and mash the kernels thoroughly. Swab the wart
with alcohol and lance the skin over the wart until a few drops of
blood appear. Dab a small amount of mashed herb on the wart. Cover
with a sterile bandage and affix with skin tape. Avoid wetting the
area. Reapply every 3-4 days.

sections.HERBS AND ACTIONS:
Pharmaceutical Latin
Pin Yin
Dosage
Actions
Rx. Rehmanniae
Sheng Di Huang
6-20g
Nourishes Yin , clears Deficiency Heat, cools the Blood and relieves toxicity.
With Xuan Shen , for Excess or Deficiency Heat patterns, late-stage febrile disease with irritability, thirst and constipation
and Kidney Yin Deficiency with Fire Blazing with soreness and swelling in the throat, dry mouth and a parched tongue.
With Xuan Shen and Mai Men Dong, for dry throat, irritability, a red tongue, and a fast thready pulse due to Devastated Yin with Blazing Fire, excessive thirst, irritability, and a scarlet tongue due to Ying Stage Heat, swelling of the throat and lymph nodes and constipation due to Excess Heat with Yin Deficiency.
With Bai Shao, for Blood Deficiency Heat.
With Mu Dan Pi, for Ying and Xue Stage Heat with a high fever, scarlet tongue, thirst, a rash all over the body, epistaxis and hemoptysis, residual Warm pathogen which has injured the Yin
and Kidney Yin Deficiency with steaming bones.
Rx. Scrophulariae
Xuan Shen
4.5-15g
Nourishes Yin , clears Deficiency Heat, cools the Blood and relieves toxicity.
With Mu Dan Pi, for erysipelas and purplish rashes.
With Sheng Di Huang, Mai Men Dong and Mu Dan Pi, for diphtheria.
Rx. Ophiopogonis
Mai Men Dong
3.6-15g
Nourishes Lung Yin , moistens the Lungs, stops cough and resolves Phlegm.
With Xuan Shen and Mu Dan Pi , for those with Yin Deficiency constitution who develop a swollen, painful diphtheria disorder after contracting an epidemic toxin.
With Sheng Di Huang, for hematemesis or epistaxis due to Yin Deficiency with Excess Heat.
With Sheng Di Huang, Xuan Shen, Mu Dan Pi and Chuan Bei Mu, for sore throat with epistaxis, hematemesis or Blood-streaked sputum and soreness and swelling of the throat due to Yin Deficiency with Excess Heat.
Dry-fried Rx. Paeoniae Alba
Chao Bai Shao
2.4-9g
Nourishes Blood and preserves and protects Yin .
Cx. Moutan
Mu Dan Pi
2.4-9g
Cools the Blood, clears Heat and reduces swelling.
Bul. Fritillariae Cirrhosae
Chuan Bei Mu
2.4-9g
Moistens the Lungs, stops cough, clears Heat and transforms Phlegm.
Hb. Menthae
Bo He
1.5-6g
Benefits the throat, clears the head and eyes, and expels Wind-Heat.
Rx. Glycyrrhizae
Gan Cao
1-6g
Relieves toxicity, benefits the throat, stops cough, harmonizes, moistens the Lungs and resolves Phlegm.

Dosage
Actions

Ma Huang

4.5-9g

3-9g

Zhi Gan Cao
2.4-6g

Sheng Jiang
4.5-6g

With Gui Zhi, strongly induces sweating for treatment of External Wind-Cold with chills, fever, body aches and anhidrosis.
With Ma Huang, strongly creates sweating to treat all externally contracted Wind-Cold disorders.

sections.CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS:
This pattern occurs in the early stages of an initial attack
or subsequent episode of guttate or plaque psoriasis.
Small coin sized red maculae located on the scalp, body, extremities,
and other areas that increase rapidly
The lesions may manifest as bright red or dark red papules,
maculopapules or macular patched of varying sizes scattered throughout
the body or distributed mostly on the trunk and limbs
Sometimes lesions start on the scalp before spreading gradually
to other parts of the body
New lesions appear continuously,
The area involved is large
There is a covered silvery-white scale
The scales are heaped up
The scales are easily shed when scratched
The scales elicit the characteristic Auspitz’s sign on
removal of the underlying moist layer.
Usually affects people under age 40
Itching may be intense
Worse during the summer
Aversion to Heat
Irritability
Restlessness
Thirst
Dry throat
Dry tongue
Bitter taste in the mouth
Dry stools
Constipation
Yellow, scanty urine
T: Red or Dark red
C: Thin yellow or white or Yellow and grimy
P: Slippery or Taut and rapid or Thin and rapid or Wiry and
rapid, or Slippery and rapid.
With Dryness :
Lesions are on the elbows, knees or lumbar area
They are reddish at the beginning
White covered lesions become fissures
Pain
T: Red
C: None or Thin yellow
P: Thready and rapid

Pin Yin
Dosage
Actions
(Honey-prepared) Rx. Astragali
(Mi Zhi) Huang Qi
10-120g
Strengthens the Spleen, raises the Yang Qi of the Spleen and Stomach , tonifies Wei Qi , s tabilizes the exterior and tonifies the Lungs (aids circulation of moisture downward from the face).
With Fang Feng, stabilizes the exterior without causing the pathogenic influences to remain.
Rz. Atractylodis Macrocephalae
Bai Zhu
9-60g
Strengthens the Spleen, tonifies Qi . stabilizes the exterior and stops sweating .
With Huang Qi , for Spleen Qi Deficiency with weakness, lassitude and loose stools.
With Huang Qi and Fang Feng, for spontaneous sweat with aversion to Wind .
Rx. Saposhnikoviae
Fang Feng
9-60g
Releases the exterior and expels External Wind.
With Huang Qi, prevents Wind from entering the skin.

sections.CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS:
Chronic simple laryngitis :
Episodic hoarseness which is most prevalent upon arising in the morning
As the physical activity increases the sound improves
The next morning the hoarseness returns
Over long periods of time there is fatigue of the voice and sound cannot be emitted for an extended period
Throat discomfort and pain upon emitting sounds
There is often a habit of clearing ones throat but no evident sputum is coughed up
The hoarseness is more evident when attempting to make a high pitched sound
Diffuse hyperemia of the laryngeal mucosa
The vocal cords have lost their original pearl white color and turned pink or progressed to a deeper red
The vertical capillaries running parallel to the border of the vocal cords are enlarged
The border is thickened
The glottis cannot be closed completely, or
The bilateral vibration is not balanced
The exterior of the vocal cords are often covered by a sticky secretion which forms sticky silk - like strands connecting the interglottic space
Chronic hypertrophic laryngitis :
Episodic hoarseness which is most prevalent upon arising in the morning
As the physical activity increases the sound improves
The next morning the hoarseness returns
Over long periods of time there is fatigue of the voice and sound cannot be emitted for an extended period
Throat discomfort and pain upon emitting sounds
There is often a habit of clearing ones throat but no evident sputum is coughed up
The hoarseness is more evident when attempting to make a high pitched sound
A long history of hoarseness and aphonia
Hoarseness is very evident
Coughing is relatively mild
Occasionally there are acute flare ups causing a further increase in hoarseness and deterioration in the sound quality
Symmetrical swelling of the laryngeal mucosa is observed but the distribution is not even and is more marked in the arythenoid space where it stands out high
When a sound is emitted it forms one or several plica in the arythenoid space
The vocal cord is thickened, appearing like a stick that is rough and not smooth and often takes on a nodular or polypoid form which is covered by a sticky secretion
If the disease progresses to the areas below the glottis, it prevents the vocal cords from uniting and triangular fissures appear
If the disease progresses to the areas below the glottis, it prevents the vocal cords from uniting and triangular fissures appear
The ventricular folds are enlarged and often press on the vocal folds when a sound is emitted
The aryepiglottic fold may also be thickened but enlargement of the epiglottis is extremely rare

sections.HERBS AND ACTIONS:
Pharmaceutical Latin
Pin Yin
Dosage
Actions
Dry-fried Fr. Aurantii Immaturus
Chao Zhi Shi
6g
Breaks up Stagnant Qi , reduces accumulation, descends Qi, u nblocks the bowels, r emoves Stagnant Food, transforms Phlegm, r educes distention and resolves hardenings .
With Hou Po, for distention, swelling and pain due to Food Stagnation and Qi Stagnation.
With Chen Pi, strengthens the Middle Jiao .
Fr. Amomi
Sha Ren
6g
Promotes the movement of Qi, aromatically transforms Dampness, strengthens the Spleen, stops vomiting, warms the Middle and stops diarrhea.
With Mu Xiang, increases the flow of Qi in the digestive system while reducing distention and Food Stagnation, alleviating pain and strengthening the Spleen.
With Mu Xiang and Zhi Shi, for Qi Stagnation due to Food Stagnation.
With Hou Po, for constrained Dampness with Qi Stagnation leading to distention and fullness in the epigastrium and abdomen.
With Chen Pi, for
Dampness obstructing the Spleen's transforming and transporting functions with reduced intake of food and diarrhea; belching, nausea, and a stifling sensation in the epigastrium due to Disharmony of the Stomach Qi
and vomiting of unadulterated, or scanty but viscous fluids.
Rz. Pinelliae Preparatum
Zhi Ban Xia
6g
Dries Dampness, expels Phlegm, descends Stomach Qi and reduces distention.
With Chen Pi , for Spleen Qi Deficiency or Phlegm-Damp Obstruction manifesting as productive cough and a stuffy chest.
With Fu Ling, expels Phlegm and stops nausea and vomiting, hiccups, coughs with clear, profuse Phlegm and loose and watery stools
and treats Phlegm, thin mucus and turbid Dampness.
With Hou Po, for Phlegm-Dampness with Qi Stagnation with a sensation of fullness in the chest with coughing and wheezing, nausea, vomiting and a sensation of distention in the hypochondrium.
Per. Citri Reticulatae
Chen Pi
6g
Revives the Spleen, activates Middle Jiao Qi , dries Dampness and transforms Phlegm.
With Zhi Ban Xia , for viscous sputum and a stuffy chest due to Phlegm-Damp Obstruction.
With Zhi Ban Xia, Hou Po and Fu Ling, enhances the Phlegm transforming, Spleen strengthening properties of the formula.
Poria
Fu Ling
6g
Strengthens the Spleen, transforms Phlegm and drains Dampness from the Middle Jiao .
With Chen Pi, for nausea, vomiting, chest fullness and distention and anorexia due to congested fluids.
With Chen Pi , Zhi Ban Xia and Sheng Jiang , for congested Fluids in the Stomach causing distention, nausea and vomiting.
With Mu Xiang, for diarrhea and borborygmus due to Dampness.
Rz. Cyperi
Xiang Fu
6g
Spreads and regulates Liver Qi and a lleviates pain .
With Sha Ren and Mu Xiang, for ulcers and digestive disturbance.
With Yan Hu Suo, for pain anywhere in the body.
Rx. Aucklandiae
Mu Xiang
1.5g
Promotes the movement of Qi , adjusts and regulates stagnant Qi in the Intestines, strengthens the Spleen, p revents Stagnation and a lleviates pain.
With Sha Ren, for distention, epigastric and abdominal pain, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysentery, or tenesmus due to Qi Obstruction and/or Food Stagnation.
Sm. Alpineae Katsumadai
Cao Dou Kou
1.5g
Dries Dampness, warms the Middle Jiao, stops vomiting and s trengthens the Spleen .
With Hou Po, for Cold-Dampness in the Middle Jiao when Dampness predominates.
With Zhi Ban Xia and Chen Pi , for Cold Phlegm affecting the chest and diaphragm with vomiting.
Dry-fried Rz. Zingiberis
Chao Gan Jiang
1.5g
Warms the Middle and e xpels Cold .
With Zhi Ban Xia, for Vomiting of saliva or dry heaves due to Cold-induced congested fluids.
With Gan Cao, for epigastric pain and vomiting due to Spleen and Stomach Deficiency Cold.
With Hou Po, for epigastric distention and pain due to Cold-induced congested fluids.
Dry-fried Cx. Magnoliae Officinalis
Chao Hou Po
2.4g
Promotes the movement of Qi in the Middle Jiao, resolves Stagnation, descends Qi, dries Dampness and transforms Phlegm.
With Gan Jiang, for acute diarrhea from Cold attacking the Middle.
With Xiang Fu and Chen Pi, for epigastric and abdominal bloating due to Dampness Obstructing the Qi.
With Zhi Ban Xia and Fu Ling, for Phlegm Obstructing the Qi , leading to coughing, vomiting or a sense of something stuck in the throat.
With Gan Jiang and Cao Dou Kou, for Cold-Dampness in the Middle Jiao .
Dry-fried Fr. Foeniculi
Chao Xiao Hui Xiang
2.4g
Warms the Liver and Kidneys, e xpels Cold, regulates Qi , h armonizes the Stomach and alleviates pain.
With Gan Jiang and Mu Xiang, for Qi Stagnation in the Middle Jiao .
Rz. Corydalis
Yan Hu Suo
2.4g
Invigorates the Blood, circulates Qi, s tops pain and induces and prolongs sleep.
Rx. Glycyrrhizae
Gan Cao
0.9g
Tonifies
the Spleen, augments Qi , r esolves Phlegm, a lleviates pain , moderates and harmonizes the harsh properties of other herbs and guides the herbs to all twelve channels .

sections.CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS:
Small coin sized red or pale red or moist pale red or dark or hyper pigmented lesions located on the scalp, body, extremities, and other areas that increase rapidly
There are covered scales which are tightly covered or heaped up and are easily shed when scratched or thick hard and adherent
Removing the scale reveals a light pink shining membrane Beneath the membrane are petechiae
Longstanding lesions may overlap
Lesions may be painful or fissured
Itching may be intense
sections.NOTES:
Put Zi Cao into a pot with 1 liter vegetable oil and bake until brown. Filter out the dregs and add powdered Huang Lian and Beeswax.
Reheat if necessary to dissolve wax.
Pour into a glass jar with an airtight lid and allow to congeal.
Apply topically 3-5 times per day.
